objective: Proof. In every Mal'tsev law, composing like cycles or not: (1) a knot is pulled back from an abelian section of its ranges (commutator theory); (2) the solutions of any system are pulled back from a linear system over the abelianizations of the variables' ranges; (3) if every abelian section is simple, every global failure on a substrate is rigid. Corollaries: every Mal'tsev law on at most three values, every non-affine one on four values, and every group law of squarefree order. Checked on random Mal'tsev algebras on three and four values.
status: Proved by TOP-LAYER-20261102-001C-P001: in every Mal'tsev law a knot is pulled back from abelian quotients of its ranges (commutator theory), a system with declared domains is pulled back from one linear system over the abelianized domains, and if every abelian section is simple every global failure on a substrate is rigid. Corollaries: all laws on three values, non-affine laws on four, group laws with prime-order sections. Mixed domains are not covered (all met were rigid); depth is necessary, not sufficient (T2(F2) rigid on regular substrates)
title: Depth is needed: simple abelian sections force rigid selection
